note: The oracle is the deployed upstream TypeScript implementation that real wallets interoperate with. That is weaker than fixtures/transparent/, whose expectations are backed by a daemon-signed transaction in fixtures/daemon/: no daemon RPC validates a VerusPayInvoice or a LoginConsentRequest, because these are wallet/application-layer formats that never enter a transaction. Upstream's tests are pure self round-trips with no hardcoded vectors, so these bytes were generated rather than copied. See fixtures/vdxf/README.md.

vectors.name: invoice_v3_basic
vectors.why: the baseline: fixed amount to a PKH destination, v3 varuint encoding

vectors.name: invoice_v3_any_amount_any_destination
vectors.why: acceptsAnyAmount and acceptsAnyDestination both suppress a field: amount and destination must be absent from the bytes, not zeroed

vectors.name: invoice_v3_accepts_conversion
vectors.why: acceptsConversion appends maxestimatedslippage after the currency id

vectors.name: invoice_v3_accepts_conversion_expires
vectors.why: expiryheight is written BEFORE maxestimatedslippage even though the expires flag (8) is a HIGHER bit than acceptsConversion (2) — field order is not flag order

vectors.name: invoice_v3_two_nonverus_systems_expires
vectors.why: acceptsNonVerusSystems appends a counted array of 20-byte hashes; the order of acceptedsystems is part of the expectation

vectors.name: invoice_v3_signed_two_nonverus_systems_expires
vectors.why: the signed path: bit 31 of the version field prepends system_id, signing_id and the signature ahead of the details

vectors.name: invoice_v4_any_amount_any_destination
vectors.why: acceptsAnyAmount and acceptsAnyDestination both suppress a field: amount and destination must be absent from the bytes, not zeroed

vectors.name: invoice_v4_accepts_conversion
vectors.why: acceptsConversion appends maxestimatedslippage after the currency id

vectors.name: invoice_v4_accepts_conversion_expires
vectors.why: expiryheight is written BEFORE maxestimatedslippage even though the expires flag (8) is a HIGHER bit than acceptsConversion (2) — field order is not flag order

vectors.why: acceptsNonVerusSystems appends a counted array of 20-byte hashes; the order of acceptedsystems is part of the expectation

vectors.name: invoice_v4_signed_sapling_destination
vectors.why: destinationIsSaplingPaymentAddress (512) swaps a 43-byte TransferDestination for an 88-byte SaplingPaymentAddress in the same field position; v4 only

vectors.name: invoice_v4_any_amount_any_destination_preconvert
vectors.why: isPreconvert (256) changes no field, only the meaning of the invoice, and is silently dropped on v3 — so it pins that the flag survives a v4 round trip

vectors.name: login_consent_request_signed
vectors.why: the signed request: system_id, signing_id and an IDENTITY_AUTH_SIG signature ahead of a challenge carrying base58 and utf-8 subjects, provisioning info, a redirect uri and a context

vectors.name: login_consent_response_signed
vectors.why: the signed response, whose signature uses a DIFFERENT vdxf key than the request's, and which embeds the whole request it answers

vectors.name: login_consent_response_one_credential
vectors.why: a Credential serialized to hex and carried in the decision context under its own vdxf key: pins the Credential encoding and the context map entry

vectors.name: login_consent_response_two_credentials
vectors.why: two credentials under two keys, the second carrying an optional label: pins the label branch and that context keys keep insertion order

vectors.name: provisioning_request_non_ascii_name
vectors.why: the requested identity name is a single emoji: pins that name is a utf-8 byte string behind a byte-count prefix, not a character count

vectors.name: provisioning_response_result_non_ascii_fqn
vectors.why: a full ProvisioningResult: every optional field present, two provisioning txids whose order is part of the expectation, and a fully qualified name whose first character is a 4-byte emoji
